dossier.summary: Orchard Row Payroll sells payroll and time tracking to restaurants and cafes with 5 to 100 staff. Pricing is a flat monthly fee plus a small amount per employee.
dossier.why_now: Added tip pooling reports this month.

data.headline: orchardrow.example sells to restaurants in its pricing page, but its homepage speaks to everyone

criteria.name: Message clarity
criteria.quote: Payroll that works the way your business does.
criteria.cost: Any business could print this line. A restaurant owner cannot tell that Orchard Row is built for kitchens and shifts, and the pricing page is where that finally shows up.

criteria.name: Proof
criteria.quote: Join the businesses that run payroll with confidence.
criteria.cost: No business is named and there is no number or review to back it up. A cautious owner reads this as a placeholder.

criteria.name: Call to action
criteria.cost: A familiar label that works. It does not say how long the trial is or that no card is needed, which are the two questions an owner has before clicking.

criteria.name: Trust
criteria.quote: Orchard Row Payroll LLC, Portland, Oregon
criteria.cost: A company name and a city are all that shows this is a real business. There is no security note, no named team and no About page link in the menu.

criteria.name: Navigation
criteria.cost: Four plain labels in a sensible order, with a page just for restaurants. It is the clearest part of the site, but the restaurant page is not mentioned on the homepage.

criteria.name: Contact path
criteria.quote: Questions? Talk to a payroll expert.
criteria.cost: A visitor who wants to talk to someone can, and the link sits right by the prices. The homepage has no such line, so only people who open pricing find it.

rewrites.before: Payroll that works the way your business does.
rewrites.after: Payroll and tip pooling for restaurants and cafes with 5 to 100 staff.
rewrites.why: Names who it is for and two things a restaurant owner cares about. An owner knows in one read that this was built for a kitchen, not an office.
Says what you get and for how long. The buyer knows what the click starts before they make it.

callouts: Could sit on any payroll site. Name restaurants and cafes in the first line, as the pricing page already does.
The line under it says confidence and ease. Replace it with what the product does in a week: run payroll, track hours, pool tips.
Start free trial is fine. Add the length of the trial so the owner knows what the click starts.
The menu is the strongest part. Link the Restaurants page from the headline area too, not only from the menu.
The proof row is a sentence with no names. Replace it with real customer names or the number of restaurants you serve.

fixes.title: Name restaurants in the headline
fixes.body: Paste the headline rewrite. The pricing page already speaks to restaurants, so the homepage only has to match it.

fixes.title: Say how long the trial is
fixes.body: Put the length of the trial and whether a card is needed on the button or right under it. Owners ask both questions before they click.

fixes.title: Add one real proof line
fixes.body: Replace Join the businesses with a count of restaurants on Orchard Row, or two named restaurants you have permission to use, with their staff size.
